# BEST THERAPY OVERALL
- Therapy class: Platinum-based doublet chemotherapy  
- Exact drug names: Carboplatin and pemetrexed  
- Reason: Absolute contraindication to immunotherapy due to diffuse interstitial lung disease (ILD), per NCCN Lung Cancer Guidelines (Version 8.2025) and ESMO Non-AGA NSCLC Metastatic Guidelines, which mandate platinum-based doublet chemotherapy as standard first-line therapy for Stage IV non-squamous NSCLC without immunotherapy eligibility. ILD significantly increases fatal immune-related pneumonitis risk, overriding biomarker considerations (including STK11 mutation). No targetable mutations (MET/BRAF/HER2 wild-type) eliminate targeted therapy options.  
- Sources: NCCN Lung Cancer Guidelines (Version 8.2025), ESMO Non-AGA NSCLC Metastatic Guidelines (2023), RAG-9LA Document (STK11 immunotherapy resistance).  

# BEST THERAPY REIMBURSED
- Therapy class: Platinum-based doublet chemotherapy  
- Exact drug names: Carboplatin and pemetrexed  
- Reason: Fully reimbursed per Italian National Health Service guidelines for first-line metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without targetable mutations. Bevacizumab excluded due to bone metastases (fracture risk) and lack of clear benefit in this context; platinum/pemetrexed alone is standard.  
- Sources: Italian National Health Service guidelines (2023).  

# CONFIDENCE
- Score: High  
- Explanation: ILD contraindication is definitive and well-documented, with no guideline-supported alternatives for this scenario.  

# EVIDENCE BASIS
- NCCN Lung Cancer Guidelines (Version 8.2025)  
- ESMO Non-AGA NSCLC Metastatic Guidelines (2023)  
- RAG-9LA Document (STK11/KEAP1/TP53 immunotherapy resistance analysis)  

# EXCLUDED THERAPIES
- Therapy class: Immunotherapy  
- Exact drug names: Pembrolizumab monotherapy  
- Reason: Absolute contraindication due to diffuse interstitial lung disease (ILD), per NCCN Lung Cancer Guidelines (Version 8.2025) and ESMO Non-AGA NSCLC Metastatic Guidelines. Immunotherapy is never recommended with ILD, regardless of biomarkers.  
- Sources: NCCN Lung Cancer Guidelines (Version 8.2025), ESMO Non-AGA NSCLC Metastatic Guidelines (2023).  

# THERAPY DOWNSIDES
- Myelosuppression (neutropenia, anemia) requiring growth factor support.  
- Fatigue, nausea, and neuropathy (manageable with supportive care).  
- Hypertension exacerbation (patient has controlled hypertension; requires monitoring but no absolute contraindication).  
- No significant increased risk from ILD (unlike immunotherapy).  

# MISSING DATA NOTES
- PD-L1 TPS (required for immunotherapy eligibility in guidelines), but irrelevant due to ILD contraindication.  
- Brain metastases status (not available), but does not change first-line therapy choice.  
- Smoking history (not available), but irrelevant for chemotherapy choice.

The Guidelines Analysis incorrectly recommended Pembrolizumab immunotherapy based on missing PD-L1 data and misreported STK11 status (reported as "no STK11/KEAP1/TP53 co-mutations" but actual data confirmed STK11 mutation). This was resolved by prioritizing absolute contraindications (ILD) per standard guidelines, which supersedes all biomarker considerations (including STK11 mutation). The ASTEP treatment selection score was invalidated due to ILD and biomarker discrepancy, and Vanguri/DLIF scores were unusable due to server errors.
